one_line: Signs an autonomous agent's execution claim with ed25519 so any mutation of the record collapses verification, behind an MIT verify() primitive.

sections.accomplishments: A named architecture with four components and a published MIT licence for the SDK; the platform pitch extends into a broader runtime-security suite described in a post-submission update.
sections.challenges: The page frames the problem (unverified logs, rejected AI-safety claims) but does not describe an engineering obstacle, a rejected alternative, or what the approach costs.
sections.how_we_built_it: Gemini 1.5 Pro at temperature 0.0 with a strict responseSchema generates the blueprint; ed25519 signs it; an MIT-licensed SDK exposes the verification primitive; the sibling submission documents a Rust engine and a GitHub Actions pipeline that rebuilds and runs a 12-scenario matrix on every change.
sections.inspiration: Enterprise AI governance is log-based: auditors reject safety claims that lack mathematical proof, and there is no way to show what an autonomous system did, why, and that the record was not edited afterwards.
sections.learned: Nothing is stated about what they would do differently.
sections.what_it_does: A claim layer: the agent's action is described in a schema-validated blueprint, signed deterministically, and any later reader can verify the bundle with a single verify() call; tampering invalidates it instantly.
sections.what_next: The update describes folding the components into one platform with a dashboard; no roadmap milestones, benchmarks or adoption targets are given.

testing: The page asserts an instant INVALID result for any mutation. That is a property of the signature scheme rather than a measurement of their system, so it is not an evaluation; no repository, workflow run, test file or corpus of mutated bundles is linked from this page.
